title: fix: handle Claude Code array output format
body:
## Problem

Claude Code recently changed its JSON output format from an object to an array. This causes `continuous-claude` to fail with jq errors:

```
jq: error (at <stdin>:1): Cannot index array with string "is_error"
jq: error (at <stdin>:1): Cannot index array with string "result"
jq: error (at <stdin>:1): Cannot index array with string "total_cost_usd"
```

## Solution

Updated all jq parsing to handle both array and object formats by:
- Checking if the type is an array using `if type == "array"`
- Accessing the last element with `.[-1]` when it's an array
- Falling back to the original object access pattern for backward compatibility

## Changes

Updated 5 locations in `continuous_claude.sh`:
- Line 894: Error extraction from JSON output
- Line 935: Error flag checking  
- Line 978: Error output display
- Line 998: Result text extraction
- Line 1018: Cost parsing

All now use the pattern: `if type == "array" then .[-1].field else .field end`

## Testing

- [x] Tested with Claude Code's new array format - jq errors resolved
- [x] Backward compatible with object format (uses fallback pattern)
- [x] All iteration outputs, error handling, and cost tracking work correctly

## Compatibility

This change is backward compatible and will work with both:
- New Claude Code versions (array format)
- Old Claude Code versions (object format)

title: Bug: PR not created when Claude commits during iteration (change detection fails)
body:
## Bug Description

When Claude Code commits changes during the main iteration (before `continuous_claude_commit` is called), the change detection logic incorrectly reports "No changes detected" and skips PR creation, even though the branch has new commits.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run continuous-claude with a prompt that causes Claude to make and commit changes
2. Observe that some iterations show "🫙 No changes detected, cleaning up branch..." 
3. But `git reflog` shows commits WERE made on those branches

## Root Cause

The `continuous_claude_commit` function (around line 611-629) only checks for **uncommitted** changes:

```bash
local has_changes=false
if ! git diff --quiet || ! git diff --cached --quiet; then
    has_changes=true
fi
# Also check for untracked files
if [ -z "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
    : # no untracked files
else
    has_changes=true
fi
```

This misses the case where Claude already committed during the iteration. The branch has commits ahead of main, but `git diff` shows nothing because there are no *uncommitted* changes.

## Evidence from Real Run

```
🔄 (1/10) Starting iteration...
🌿 (1/10) Creating branch: continuous-claude/iteration-1/2025-11-25-4be53a4b
🤖 (1/10) Running Claude Code...
📝 (1/10) Output:
Added a `/dice` endpoint...
CONTINUOUS_CLAUDE_PROJECT_COMPLETE
🎯 (1/10) Completion signal detected (1/3)
💰 (1/10) Cost: $0.216
✅ (1/10) Work completed
🫙 (1/10) No changes detected, cleaning up branch...  ← BUG: Changes were committed!
```

But `git reflog` showed:
```
8a239f9 HEAD@{9}: commit: Add dice roller endpoint with NdM notation  ← Commit exists!
ec79e2e HEAD@{10}: checkout: moving from main to continuous-claude/iteration-1/2025-11-25-4be53a4b
```

## Fix

Add a check for committed changes by comparing the branch to main:

```bash
continuous_claude_commit() {
    local iteration_display="$1"
    local branch_name="$2"
    local main_branch="$3"

    if ! git rev-parse --git-dir > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        return 0
    fi

    # Check for uncommitted changes
    local has_uncommitted_changes=false
    if ! git diff --quiet || ! git diff --cached --quiet; then
        has_uncommitted_changes=true
    fi
    if [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
        has_uncommitted_changes=true
    fi

    # Check if there are committed changes on this branch compared to main
    # This handles the case where Claude already committed during the iteration
    local has_committed_changes=false
    local commits_ahead=$(git rev-list --count "$main_branch".."$branch_name" 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
    if [ "$commits_ahead" -gt 0 ]; then
        has_committed_changes=true
    fi

    # If no uncommitted changes AND no committed changes, nothing to do
    if [ "$has_uncommitted_changes" = "false" ] && [ "$has_committed_changes" = "false" ]; then
        echo "🫙 $iteration_display No changes detected, cleaning up branch..." >&2
        git checkout "$main_branch" >/dev/null 2>&1
        git branch -D "$branch_name" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
        return 0
    fi

    # If Claude already committed, skip the commit step but continue to PR
    if [ "$has_uncommitted_changes" = "false" ] && [ "$has_committed_changes" = "true" ]; then
        echo "📦 $iteration_display Changes already committed on branch: $branch_name ($commits_ahead commit(s) ahead)" >&2
    fi
    
    # ... rest of function, but wrap the commit step:
    
    # Only run the commit step if there are uncommitted changes
    if [ "$has_uncommitted_changes" = "true" ]; then
        echo "💬 $iteration_display Committing changes..." >&2
        # ... existing commit logic ...
    fi
    
    # ... continue with push and PR creation ...
}
```

## After Fix

```
🔄 (1/10) Starting iteration...
🌿 (1/10) Creating branch: continuous-claude/iteration-1/2025-11-25-02b37fc3
🤖 (1/10) Running Claude Code...
📝 (1/10) Output:
Added a **Magic 8-Ball endpoint**...
CONTINUOUS_CLAUDE_PROJECT_COMPLETE
🎯 (1/10) Completion signal detected (1/3)
💰 (1/10) Cost: $0.189
✅ (1/10) Work completed
💬 (1/10) Committing changes...
📦 (1/10) Changes committed on branch: continuous-claude/iteration-1/2025-11-25-02b37fc3
📤 (1/10) Pushing branch...
🔨 (1/10) Creating pull request...
🔍 (1/10) PR #5 created...  ← Now works correctly!
✅ (1/10) PR merged and local branch cleaned up
```

I can submit a PR with the complete fix if you'd like.

title: Smarter retries
body:
Currently, if the commit command fails, then it restarts the entire loop. But instead, it should retry only the commit command first with an exponential backoff a few times, and only after that, it should start a new loop iteration. 

Similarly, I saw this error once:

```
⚠️  (5/22) Failed to create PR: GraphQL: API rate limit already exceeded for user ID 2841780.
```

and it continued to the next iteration when instead it should wait for rate limits and retry only the "gh" command first, and after a few retries fail.

## Changes

- **New `detect_github_repo()` function**: Parses git remote URL to extract owner/repo
  - Supports HTTPS (`https://github.com/owner/repo.git`) and SSH (`git@github.com:owner/repo.git`) formats
  - Handles URLs with or without `.git` suffix
  
- **Updated `validate_arguments()`**: Auto-detects missing values before validation
  - Explicit flags take precedence over auto-detection
  - Clear error messages when detection fails: "Use --owner to provide the owner, or run from a git repository with a GitHub remote"

- **Updated help and README**: Flags now shown as optional with auto-detection note

## Usage

```bash
# Before: always required
continuous-claude -p "add tests" -m 5 --owner user --repo project

# After: optional when in a git repo with GitHub remote
continuous-claude -p "add tests" -m 5

# Still works explicitly for non-git directories or non-GitHub remotes
continuous-claude -p "add tests" -m 5 --owner user --repo project
```

Adds `--max-duration` flag to run continuous-claude in time-boxed bursts, complementing existing `--max-runs` and `--max-cost` limits.

## Changes

- **Duration parsing**: `parse_duration()` converts human-readable strings ("2h", "30m", "1h30m") to seconds with case-insensitive, whitespace-tolerant parsing
- **Duration formatting**: `format_duration()` converts seconds back to human-readable format for display
- **Flag handling**: Added `--max-duration` to argument parsing and validation, accepts format alternatives to `--max-runs`/`--max-cost`
- **Time tracking**: `main_loop()` tracks start time and checks elapsed duration before each iteration, stops when limit reached
- **User feedback**: Completion summary displays elapsed time when duration limit used

## Usage

```bash
# Run for 2 hours
continuous-claude -p "Add tests" --max-duration 2h

# Run for 30 minutes
continuous-claude -p "Refactor" --max-duration 30m

# Combine with cost limit (whichever hits first)
continuous-claude -p "Improve code" --max-duration 1h --max-cost 5.00
```

Supports hours (h/H), minutes (m/M), seconds (s/S) in any combination. Rejects zero and invalid formats with clear error messages.

title: Add adaptive rate limiting with leaky-bucket governor
body:
Implements rate limiting to prevent API thrashing when running continuous Claude iterations. Tracks calls and errors per hour using a leaky-bucket algorithm, with configurable ceilings and automatic backoff.

## New CLI Flags

- `--max-calls-per-hour <num>`: Caps Claude API calls per hour; sleeps when bucket fills
- `--error-threshold <num>`: Triggers exponential backoff when error count exceeds threshold

## Implementation

- **Leaky-bucket rate limiter**: Sliding 1-hour window tracking call timestamps; waits until oldest call expires when at capacity
- **Error threshold backoff**: Progressive backoff (1 min per error over threshold, capped at 30 min)
- **Claude rate limit detection**: Recognizes "Session limit reached ∙ resets 7pm", "429", "quota exceeded", etc. and parses reset time
- **Dashboard output**: `⏱️ (1/5) Throttled for 4m (limit 80/80 per hour)`

## Usage

```bash
# Limit to 80 calls per hour
continuous-claude -p "Add tests" -m 100 --max-calls-per-hour 80

# Backoff after 5 errors per hour  
continuous-claude -p "Fix bugs" -m 50 --error-threshold 5

# Combine with other limits
continuous-claude -p "Add features" --max-duration 4h --max-calls-per-hour 60 --error-threshold 3
```

Rate limit errors from Claude are detected and handled separately—they trigger smart backoff without counting toward the consecutive error limit that would otherwise terminate the run.

title: Feature Request: Native Windows Support (PowerShell)
body:
## Feature Request: Native Windows Support

### Problem
Currently, `continuous-claude` is a bash shell script that doesn't run natively on Windows. Windows users need to use WSL or Git Bash, which adds friction and complexity to the setup process.

### Proposed Solution
Add native Windows support via one of these approaches:

1. **PowerShell version** (`continuous-claude.ps1`) - A native PowerShell implementation that works directly in Windows Terminal/PowerShell
2. **Cross-platform Node.js version** - Rewrite in Node.js which runs on all platforms
3. **Go/Rust binary** - Compile to native executables for Windows/Mac/Linux

### Benefits
- Simpler setup for Windows users (no WSL/Git Bash required)
- Better integration with Windows development workflows
- Broader adoption among Windows developers

### Current Workaround
Windows users must:
1. Install WSL or use Git Bash
2. Set up symlinks to Windows tools (claude.exe, gh.exe, jq.exe)
3. Run via `wsl bash -l -c "..."` which is cumbersome

### Environment
- Windows 10/11
- PowerShell 7.x
- Claude Code CLI works natively on Windows

Would love to see native Windows support! Happy to help test if a Windows version is developed.

title: feat: Add --wait flag to wait for session limit reset
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a `-w|--wait` flag that enables automatic waiting when Claude CLI returns a session limit message like "Session limit reached ∙ resets 7pm".

- **Detects** session limit messages in stderr or JSON error output
- **Parses** reset times (supports "7pm", "7:30pm", "7 PM", "10am", etc.)
- **Waits** until the reset time + configurable buffer (default 10 seconds)
- **Retries** the iteration automatically without counting it as an error

This is especially useful for users on cheaper plans who regularly need to wait for their credits to reset. Instead of the script failing and requiring manual intervention, it will wait and continue automatically.

### Example usage

```bash
# Wait for session limit to reset instead of failing
continuous-claude -p "Long running task" --max-cost 50.00 --wait

# Prevent system sleep during wait (macOS)
caffeinate -i continuous-claude -p "Long task" --max-cost 50.00 --wait
```

### Key implementation details

- Session limit errors don't increment the consecutive error counter (not counted toward the 3-error fatal limit)
- Midnight rollover is handled (if reset time is in the past, assumes next day)
- Uses simple sleep - users can wrap with `caffeinate -i` on macOS to prevent sleep during long waits
- Buffer time is configurable in source (`WAIT_BUFFER_SECONDS=10`)

### Related

Related to #36 (rate limiting) - while that PR dealt with signalling a stop condition via rate limit detection, this feature optionally allows waiting until the parsed local reset time before continuing.

## Test plan

- [x] Added 20 new tests covering:
  - Argument parsing for `-w`/`--wait` flag
  - Time parsing (7pm, 7:30pm, 7 PM, 10am, invalid, empty)
  - Session limit detection (standard, with minutes, usage limit, hour limit, case insensitivity)
  - Wait mode behavior (disabled vs enabled)
  - Help text verification

title: Misleading “PR merge queue failed” error on private repos with GitHub plan restrictions
body:
Hi,

I’m running continuous-claude against a private GitHub repository and consistently hit the following error during runs that create commits/PRs:

> PR merge queue failed (1 consecutive errors)

The issue disappears completely when using `--disable-commits`.

After debugging, this does not seem to be an actual “merge queue” problem but rather an API/feature restriction that is surfaced with a misleading error message.

Findings:
- Repository is private
- I have ADMIN permissions
- Default branch is main
- GitHub REST API calls return 403 for:
  - /repos/<owner>/<repo>/rulesets
  - /repos/<owner>/<repo>/branches/main/protection
  with message: “Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public to enable this feature.”

Environment:
- continuous-claude v0.18.0
- git 2.51.0
- gh 2.46.0
- Ubuntu 25.10
- Repo private, ADMIN permissions

Expected behavior:
- Surface real GitHub 403 errors caused by plan limitations
- Do not label these cases as “merge queue failed”

Workaround:
Using --disable-branches avoids the issue.

Suggestion:
Improve error handling and consider a mode to create PRs without merging.

Thanks for the great tool — this would make debugging much clearer in private-repo setups.

title: Add explicit no-commit instructions to workflow and reviewer prompts
body:
Agents may attempt to commit/push changes in the main workflow and reviewer contexts, creating confusion since automation handles this after completion.

## Changes

Added explicit `**Do NOT commit or push changes**` instruction to:
- `PROMPT_WORKFLOW_CONTEXT` - Tells agent to focus on code changes only
- `PROMPT_REVIEWER_CONTEXT` - Tells agent to focus on validation/fixes only

The `PROMPT_CI_FIX_CONTEXT` intentionally retains its instruction to commit, as it updates existing PRs directly.

## Context

The workflow runs agents in sequence:
1. Main iteration (uses `PROMPT_WORKFLOW_CONTEXT`)
2. Optional reviewer pass (uses `PROMPT_REVIEWER_CONTEXT`)
3. Automation commits/pushes via `PROMPT_COMMIT_MESSAGE`

Without explicit instructions in steps 1-2, agents may incorrectly attempt git operations that interfere with step 3.

title: :bug: Fix commit verification with dirty submodules
body:
Commit verification fails when submodules have uncommitted content, blocking iteration progress. Users with `diff.ignoreSubmodules=none` or similar configurations hit this consistently.

## Changes

Added `--ignore-submodules=dirty` to `git diff` commands in commit verification:

- `continuous_claude_commit()`: Initial change detection (L1186-1187) and post-commit verification (L1223)
- `commit_on_current_branch()`: Initial change detection (L1321-1322) and post-commit verification (L1348)

This overrides user git config and ensures dirty submodules don't block commits of parent repo changes.

```bash
# Before: Failed if user had diff.ignoreSubmodules=none
if ! git diff --quiet || ! git diff --cached --quiet; then

# After: Ignores dirty submodules regardless of config
if ! git diff --quiet --ignore-submodules=dirty || ! git diff --cached --quiet --ignore-submodules=dirty; then
```

## Testing

Added tests simulating parent repo changes with dirty submodules present.

title: Add rate limiting support to handle Claude API token limits and auto-resume tasks
body:
## Problem

When Claude Code hits a token/rate limit during a continuous-claude iteration, the script would fail and stop, requiring manual intervention to resume the task once tokens reset.

## Solution

This PR adds automatic rate limiting support that:

1. Detects when Claude hits a rate limit
2. Parses the reset time from Claude's response (supports formats like "resets 8pm" and ISO timestamps)
3. Automatically waits until tokens reset
4. Sends a "Continue" command to resume the interrupted task

## Changes

- Added `check_rate_limit()` function with smart time parsing
- Added `parse_reset_time()` to handle various time formats (ISO, "8pm", etc.)
- Added CLI flags: `--no-rate-limit`, `--rate-limit-interval`, `--rate-limit-max-wait`, `--rate-limit-fallback`
- Added rate limit detection in error handling
- Added CONTRIBUTING.md with guidelines

## Testing

- Verified rate limit detection with actual rate-limited account
- Confirmed time parsing works for "8pm" format on macOS
- Tested fallback behavior when parsing fails

```
adityakarnam@MacBookPro-5805 continuous-claude % ./continuous_claude.sh -p "Update the README for the project" -m 1
⚠️  Rate limit check command failed, proceeding anyway
🔄 (1/1) Starting iteration...
🌿 (1/1) Creating branch: continuous-claude/iteration-1/2026-02-21-1bfe56ee
🤖 (1/1) Running Claude Code...
   (1/1) 💬 You've hit your limit · resets 8pm (America/Chicago)
You've hit your limit · resets 8pm (America/Chicago)

⚠️  Claude Code command failed with exit code: 1

⚠️ (1/1) Rate limit error detected in iteration
🔄 (1/1) Sleeping 1239 minutes until reset at 2026-02-22 20:00:07...
```

## Example

```bash
# Default - rate limiting enabled
continuous-claude -p "long task" -m 10

# With custom check interval
continuous-claude -p "task" -m 5 --rate-limit-interval 60000

# Disable rate limiting
continuous-claude -p "quick task" -m 3 --no-rate-limit
```

title: :bug: Synchronize provider stderr capture
body:
## Summary
- fixes a race where provider stderr could be inspected before the asynchronous `tee` process had written it
- uses a FIFO plus an explicitly awaited `tee` process for both Claude and Codex providers
- keeps stderr streaming live while guaranteeing complete error-log capture
- refreshes the tracked Bash script checksum

## Root cause
Post-merge Create Release CI for #65 failed twice in the existing `run_agent_iteration captures Codex stderr to error log` regression. The mocked Codex process wrote `Codex auth failed`, but the generic `wait` did not reliably wait for the pipeline's process substitution, so the code saw an empty stderr file and generated its fallback message instead.

## Test plan

- [x] FIFO synchronization micro-reproduction passed 100/100 iterations
- [x] Claude/Codex stderr-capture regressions passed 20 consecutive runs
